title: Believest Thou This?
summary: William Branham preaches on the resurrection of Lazarus from John 11, emphasizing the importance of taking God at His Word without waiting for signs. He contrasts the faith of Mary with the doubt of Zacharias, and discusses the foreordination of gifts and the need for a fresh daily infilling of the Holy Ghost.

title: At Thy Word
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of faith and the power of God's Word, sharing testimonies of healings and a supernatural photograph. He emphasizes that healing comes through faith in Christ and encourages believers to launch out into the deep at God's Word.

title: Believest Thou This?
summary: William Branham speaks on faith and divine healing, emphasizing that healing is already provided through Christ's atonement. He uses the story of Mary and the angel Gabriel to illustrate taking God at His Word without signs, and encourages believers to accept healing by faith.

title: Believe Ye That I Am Able To Do This?
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of faith in Jesus Christ to heal, using the biblical account of two blind men and a deaf-mute. He shares testimonies of miraculous healings, including a woman raised from a coma and a blind girl receiving sight, emphasizing that faith in Christ, not human effort, brings healing.

title: The Works That I Do Bear Witness of Me
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of unity among believers and the love of God, emphasizing that faith without works is dead. He calls for breaking down denominational barriers and loving one another as evidence of true discipleship. The sermon also includes a call to seek the Giver before the gifts and a testimony of the Angel of the Lord's guidance.

title: Believest Thou This?
summary: William Branham speaks on faith and healing, using the resurrection of Lazarus as a text. He shares personal testimony of his ministry and the physical and mental strain of spiritual work, encouraging believers to trust God even in the last moment.

title: Faith Is the Substance
summary: William Branham teaches on faith as the substance of things hoped for, emphasizing that divine healing is already provided in the atonement and must be accepted by faith. He explains that faith is a real sense of the inward man, distinct from the five physical senses, and that healing comes through believing in what Jesus has already done. The sermon includes a call for ministers to pray for the sick and a demonstration of the gift of discernment as a sign of God's presence.
themes: The inward man vs. outward senses

title: Our Hope Is In God
summary: William Branham speaks on the hope of the Church being in God alone, not in human power or weapons. He shares testimonies of healings and visions, including a boy raised from the dead in Finland and his own baby's healing, demonstrating that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

title: For Him Will I Accept
summary: William Branham speaks on the power of prayer and the importance of unity among believers, using the story of Job to illustrate how God honors the prayers of the righteous. He emphasizes that healing is already provided through Christ's sacrifice and encourages the audience to believe and receive their healing.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses divine healing, the atonement, and the importance of faith, using biblical examples such as the healing at the pool of Bethesda and the woman at the well to illustrate how Jesus only did what the Father showed Him.
themes: the role of visions in ministry

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that healing was accomplished at Calvary and that believers must accept it by faith. He demonstrates the gift of discernment as a confirmation of Christ's presence, and prays for the sick, urging them to believe in the finished work of Christ.
themes: Christ the same yesterday, today, and forever
The Word of God defeats Satan

title: Show Us The Father And It'll Satisfy Us
summary: William Branham speaks on the deep human longing to see God, using nature, Scripture, and personal experience to reveal God's presence. He emphasizes that God is visible in His creation, His Word, His Son, and His people, and that true satisfaction comes from seeing the Father through faith.

title: Faith
summary: William Branham speaks on faith, using the Exodus account of God sending an angel before Israel to illustrate that God's promises are already given and must be possessed by faith. He shares personal experiences of divine intervention and healing, emphasizing the need to abide in Christ and reject unbelief.

title: Do You Now Believe?
summary: In this closing sermon of a Phoenix campaign, William Branham expresses gratitude to supporters and shares testimonies of healing. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and calls the congregation to believe in His resurrection power. The sermon includes a vision of a future overseas revival and a prayer for the sick.
themes: Unity in the body of Christ

title: What Think Ye of Christ?
summary: William Branham preaches on the deity of Jesus Christ, asking the question 'What think ye of Christ?' He examines testimonies from biblical figures, enemies, friends, and hymn writers to affirm that Jesus is the virgin-born Son of God. Branham emphasizes that one's attitude toward Christ determines their eternal destiny.

title: Earnestly Contending for the Faith
summary: William Branham preaches on Jude's exhortation to earnestly contend for the faith once delivered to the saints. He contrasts the early church's power and unity with modern denominational divisions and spiritual decline, urging a return to apostolic faith marked by signs, wonders, and holiness.

title: IT IS I, BE NOT AFRAID
summary: William Branham preaches on Jesus walking on water, emphasizing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages believers not to be afraid of supernatural manifestations, as they are signs of Jesus' presence and power to heal and save.

title: Sirs, Be of a Good Cheer
summary: William Branham encourages the congregation to have faith in God's promises, using the account of Paul's shipwreck in Acts 27. He prays over prayer cloths, shares a testimony of a vision about Brother Bosworth, and ministers healing through the gift of discernment.

title: Melchisedec, The Great Prince And King
summary: William Branham teaches on the assurance of faith based on God's immutable promises, using Hebrews 6-7 and Genesis 14. He emphasizes that God swore by Himself to bless Abraham and his Seed, Christ, and that believers have an anchor of the soul within the veil through Jesus, a high priest after the order of Melchisedec.

title: Beginning and Ending of the Gentile Dispensation
summary: William Branham preaches on the Gentile dispensation from Daniel's prophecies, emphasizing the rise and fall of Gentile kingdoms, the coming of Christ as the Stone cut without hands, and the signs of the end times including the restoration of Israel and the outpouring of the Holy Spirit.

title: The Fundamental Foundation for Faith
summary: William Branham preaches on the foundational basis for faith, explaining that man was originally created to have dominion over all things but lost that through the fall. Through Christ's redemption, believers are restored to that original state and can operate in faith when they abide in Christ and His Word. He emphasizes that faith is an unconscious trust in God's Word, and that the Holy Spirit works through believers to manifest the same works Jesus did.

title: Doctor Moses
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical account of Moses lifting up the brass serpent in the wilderness as a type of Christ's crucifixion. He emphasizes that healing and salvation come through spiritual revelation and faith in God's Word, not through human effort or psychology. Branham also shares testimonies of healings and encourages the congregation to seek a genuine revival through repentance and confession.
themes: Typology of Christ in the Old Testament

title: Law
summary: William Branham preaches on the law as a shadow of good things to come, contrasting the imperfect sacrifices of the Old Testament with the perfect and final sacrifice of Jesus Christ. He emphasizes that true perfection comes through faith in Christ's blood, which cleanses sin and transforms the believer, and warns against willful unbelief as the unpardonable sin.

title: The Believer's Position in Christ
subtitle: 55-0116A
summary: William Branham teaches on the believer's position in Christ, emphasizing that believers are chosen before the foundation of the world and must be in Christ through the Blood to worship God. He uses the Old Testament tabernacle and the story of Moses to illustrate God's timing and the need for direct revelation. The sermon concludes with the concept of adoption into God's family, where believers are given authority and a specific ministry.

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham speaks on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He shares testimonies of healings and deliverances, and calls the congregation to faith in Christ's finished work at Calvary.

title: How The Angel Came To Me, And His Commission
summary: William Branham recounts his early life and the supernatural experiences that shaped his ministry, including visions, an encounter with Jesus, and the commissioning by an angel. He emphasizes that gifts and callings are without repentance and shares lessons learned about discerning true spirituality.

title: This Great Warrior, David
summary: William Branham preaches on David as a type of the believer who is elected, called, anointed, and placed in Christ. He contrasts David's faith with Israel's reliance on outward appearances and human wisdom, urging believers to trust God's Word and their position in Christ.

title: This Great Warrior, Joshua
summary: William Branham preaches on Joshua as a type of Christ and the believer's position in God. He contrasts the faith of Joshua and Caleb with the unbelief of Israel at Kadesh-Barnea, drawing parallels to the modern church's hesitation to fully embrace the Holy Spirit and divine healing. Branham emphasizes that God's promises are sure and that believers must fight spiritually to possess their inheritance.

title: The Seven Compound Names of Jehovah
summary: William Branham preaches on the seven compound names of Jehovah, focusing on Jehovah-jireh (the Lord will provide a sacrifice) and Jehovah-shammah (the Lord is present). He emphasizes that God is always present to fulfill His redemptive promises, using the story of Abraham and Isaac as a type of Christ's sacrifice.

title: The Water of Separation
summary: William Branham preaches on the Old Testament type of the red heifer and the water of separation, showing how it prefigures Christ's sacrifice and the cleansing power of the Word. He emphasizes that life comes through death, and that believers are separated from sin and sickness by applying the Word of God. The sermon concludes with a healing service where Branham demonstrates the gift of discernment.

title: This Great Servant, Moses
summary: William Branham preaches on the life of Moses, focusing on the rod of judgment as a type of Christ. He draws parallels between Moses' rod and the cross, emphasizing that Christ bore judgment for sin and sickness. The sermon encourages believers to speak to the Rock, Christ Jesus, for healing and deliverance.

title: The Approach to God
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of approaching God through His provided way, which is the shed blood of Jesus Christ. He contrasts man's self-made approaches with God's ordained method, using examples from Adam, Job, Abraham, and Israel. The sermon emphasizes that only through the blood sacrifice can one have an audience with God and receive His blessings.
themes: El Shaddai as the all-sufficient One

title: Earnestly Contend for the Faith
summary: William Branham preaches on Jude 3, urging believers to earnestly contend for the faith once delivered to the saints. He contrasts the original apostolic faith—characterized by signs, wonders, and divine revelation—with modern denominational divisions, emphasizing that true Christianity is the life of Christ reproduced in believers through the Holy Spirit.

title: The Second Coming
summary: William Branham opens a revival meeting in Phoenix, discussing his ministry policies, the importance of preaching the Gospel to all the world, and sharing experiences from his missionary trip to India. He emphasizes that the Gospel must be accompanied by the power and demonstration of the Holy Spirit, and expresses his belief that the second coming of Christ is near.

title: Contend For The Faith
summary: William Branham opens a series of meetings, emphasizing that healing and salvation come through faith in the finished work of Christ, not human power. He explains the gift of discernment and visions as a means to build faith, and urges believers to contend for the faith once delivered to the saints, as exemplified by Jesus' ministry of supernatural knowledge and healing.
themes: God's attitude toward sinners and sick

title: Christ
summary: William Branham preaches on Christ as the fulfillment of Old Testament types, focusing on the red heifer sacrifice in Numbers 19 as a symbol of Christ's blood for redemption and purification. He emphasizes that fellowship with God is only possible through the shed blood of Jesus, and calls believers to come to the waters of separation—the Word—and enter into the blood for true fellowship and power.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on the redemptive name Jehovah-Jireh, emphasizing God's provision and the unconditional covenant with Abraham. He encourages faith in God's promises, drawing from the story of Abraham and Isaac, and calls believers to trust in El Shaddai, the all-sufficient God.

title: Job
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of redemption, using the story of Job as a central example. He emphasizes that redemption was planned before the foundation of the world and is accomplished through the shed blood of Christ, the Lamb of God. Branham encourages believers to trust in God's provided way of redemption and to live in the freedom that Christ has secured.

title: Water From The Rock
summary: William Branham preaches on the Old Testament story of Moses striking the rock at Meribah, using it as a lesson about obeying God's specific instructions. He contrasts his own healing ministry with others, emphasizing the need to find the cause of sickness before the cure. He also discusses the journey of Israel as a type of the church, the importance of following the Spirit, and the danger of grumbling and division among believers.

title: Glorified Jesus
summary: William Branham speaks on the spiritual revelation of Jesus Christ as the foundation of the Church, using Matthew 16:15-18 as a text. He contrasts the offerings of Cain and Abel to illustrate that true faith comes from divine revelation, not human effort. The sermon emphasizes the hope of resurrection and being buried in Christ.

title: The Position Of A Believer In Christ
summary: William Branham shares about a powerful healing meeting with Apache Indians, then teaches on the believer's position in Christ, emphasizing that true faith comes from being baptized by the Holy Spirit into Christ's body, bearing the fruit of the Spirit, and working in harmony with God's laws.
themes: fruit of the Spirit vs. gifts of the Spirit

title: The Healing of Jairus' Daughter
summary: William Branham preaches on the healing of Jairus' daughter, emphasizing faith in Christ's atonement and the power of the Holy Spirit. He contrasts the Old Testament sacrificial system with Christ's sacrifice, which imparts eternal life through the Holy Spirit. Branham encourages believers to touch Jesus by faith, regardless of opposition or doubt.
themes: the Holy Spirit as the life of Christ

title: Separation from Unbelief
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of separating from unbelief and worldly associations, using the biblical account of Jehoshaphat's alliance with the wicked king Jehoram as a cautionary example. He emphasizes that true faith comes from the heart through the Holy Spirit, not from intellectual knowledge, and warns against being unequally yoked with unbelievers.
themes: The Holy Spirit's role in healing

title: The Resurrected Lord Jesus
summary: William Branham speaks on the resurrected Lord Jesus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages believers to have faith in God's healing power and shares personal testimonies of God's intervention.

title: The Seal Of The Antichrist
summary: William Branham preaches on the seal of the antichrist, warning against religious spirits that mimic true Christianity. He emphasizes that outward signs like speaking in tongues or shouting do not guarantee salvation; only receiving the Person of Jesus Christ and bearing the fruits of the Spirit matter. Using the Old Testament type of the Hebrew servant who chose to remain in bondage, he illustrates how rejecting truth leads to being sealed out of God's Kingdom.

title: The Seal of the Christ
summary: William Branham contrasts the seal of the Antichrist with the seal of Christ, emphasizing that the true seal of God is the Holy Spirit, which produces the fruit of the Spirit in believers. He warns against mere religious formality and emotionalism, stressing that only those who sigh and cry over the abominations in the city receive God's seal.
themes: Seal of God vs. seal of the beast
Fruit of the Spirit as evidence of salvation
Rejection of truth leads to judgment

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham uses the story of blind Bartimaeus to illustrate God's provision through the Lamb of God, Jesus Christ. He emphasizes that healing and salvation are already accomplished at Calvary and are received by faith. Branham testifies to the present ministry of Jesus through the Holy Spirit, evidenced by supernatural signs and visions.

title: Fellowship By Redemption
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of fellowship with God through redemption. He shares testimonies of healings from recent meetings, announces plans for a healing service and baptism on Easter Sunday, and teaches that true fellowship with God requires a new foundation in Christ, not mere reformation. He emphasizes that faith must go beyond intellectual acceptance to a born-again experience.
themes: The Word of God as eternal truth
The presence of God in the believer

title: My Redeemer Liveth
summary: In this Easter sermon, William Branham celebrates the resurrection of Jesus Christ as the central hope of Christianity. He contrasts the empty rituals of dead religion with the living assurance that comes from experiencing the resurrected Christ personally. Drawing on Job's declaration 'I know my Redeemer liveth,' he calls believers to move beyond mere hope to a confident 'know-so' faith.

title: Proof of His Resurrection
summary: William Branham delivers an Easter sermon emphasizing the resurrection of Jesus Christ as a present reality, not just a historical event. He argues that the Holy Spirit's work in believers, including healing and spiritual gifts, provides infallible proof that Christ is alive today. Branham calls for a personal experience of the resurrection through faith and the new birth, moving beyond tradition and intellectual belief.

title: Prayer
subtitle: 55-0410E
summary: William Branham offers a prayer of thanksgiving for the privilege of coming to God, for the hope of resurrection, and for the church and its members. He asks for God's blessing on the service and for the Word to be planted in hearts.

title: Fellowship
summary: William Branham speaks on the theme of fellowship with God and with one another, emphasizing that true fellowship is only possible through the blood of Jesus Christ. He contrasts this with denominational divisions and worldly substitutes, urging believers to return to a blood-bought revival and a carefree trust in God.

title: The Faith That Was Once Delivered to the Saints
summary: William Branham speaks on the faith that was once delivered to the saints, emphasizing that true faith is a direct revelation from God, not intellectual belief. He uses examples from the Bible, such as Abel, Peter, and the woman at the well, to illustrate that this faith is accompanied by signs and wonders. Branham also shares personal anecdotes and reflects on the passing of Brother Ryan.

title: The Ark
summary: William Branham teaches on the typology of the ark in the Old Testament, showing how Noah's ark, Moses' basket, and the ark of the covenant all foreshadow Christ as the ultimate ark of salvation. He emphasizes that believers are sealed by the Holy Spirit and protected from judgment through the atonement of Christ's blood.

title: Jairus, A Secret Believer
summary: William Branham speaks on faith based on God's Word, using the story of Jairus as a secret believer who sought Jesus for his dying daughter. He emphasizes that prayer changes things and that true faith rests on God's promises, not human reasoning.

title: Fellowship Through The Reconciliation of The Blood
summary: William Branham speaks on the necessity of fellowship with God through the blood of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that true fellowship is not found in church membership, education, or good works, but only through the shed blood of Christ. He uses the examples of Adam and Eve, Cain and Abel, and Job to illustrate that reconciliation with God requires a spiritual revelation and acceptance of God's provided sacrifice.

title: The Waters of Separation
summary: William Branham preaches on the Old Testament type of the red heifer and the waters of separation, showing how it prefigures Christ's sacrifice and the cleansing power of the Word. He emphasizes that the Word is the waters of separation that cleanses believers from sin and sickness, and calls for a heart-faith rather than mere intellectual assent.

title: The True Vine and a False Vine
summary: William Branham contrasts the true vine (Abel's line) with the false vine (Cain's line), tracing these two spirits through Scripture from Genesis to the end times. He warns against religious sincerity without divine revelation and emphasizes that the true church is marked by the supernatural power of the Holy Spirit, not by organization or intellectual theology.
themes: The church's departure from supernatural faith

title: Abraham
summary: William Branham speaks on the faith of Abraham, emphasizing God's sovereign election and the importance of taking God at His Word regardless of circumstances. He recounts the debate in Houston where the Angel of the Lord was photographed, and explains the covenant God made with Abraham as a type of the New Covenant in Christ.

title: A Greater Witness Than John
summary: William Branham preaches on the greater witness of Jesus Christ compared to John the Baptist, emphasizing that Jesus' works bear witness of Him. He shares a testimony of being led by the Holy Spirit to pray for a dying man in Memphis, and then ministers to the sick with the gift of discernment.

title: DO YOU NOW BELIEVE?
summary: William Branham speaks on the power of love and faith in healing, sharing personal testimonies of miracles and the importance of creating an atmosphere of belief. He emphasizes that God's presence brings healing and encourages the congregation to trust in God's Word.

title: The Presence of the Lord Jesus
summary: William Branham speaks at the close of a revival meeting in Macon, Georgia, sharing testimonies of healings and a resurrection in Finland. He emphasizes the presence of Jesus Christ and the importance of faith, using the story of Lazarus to illustrate that Jesus is the resurrection and the life.

title: Contending For The Faith
summary: William Branham preaches on Jude 1:3, urging believers to earnestly contend for the faith once delivered to the saints. He emphasizes that true faith rests on God's Word, not creeds or denominations, and demonstrates the same works of Jesus through the Holy Spirit, including healing and discernment.
themes: the Word of God as foundation

title: The Roman Nobleman
summary: William Branham preaches on the faith of the Roman centurion who believed Jesus could heal his servant with just a word. He emphasizes that healing comes through faith in Christ's finished work at Calvary, not through any human power. Branham then demonstrates the gift of discernment by calling out specific ailments and conditions in the audience, leading many to receive healing.

title: Abraham
summary: William Branham speaks on the faith of Abraham, emphasizing that God's promises are seeds that produce when received without unbelief. He connects Abraham's encounter with God in Genesis 18 to the ministry of Jesus and the present-day manifestation of God's power through visions and healings.

title: Show Us The Father
summary: William Branham preaches on seeing God in His creation, His Word, His Son, and His people. He encourages faith and healing, demonstrating the Holy Spirit's presence through prayer and discernment.

title: My Life Story
summary: William Branham shares his personal testimony, from his humble birth in a log cabin to his call to ministry. He recounts the hardships of his early life, the loss of his wife and daughter, and his commitment to preach the Gospel despite persecution.

title: I Will Restore
subtitle: 55-0626E
summary: William Branham preaches on the restoration of the church, contrasting the spirit of Cain (formalism, dead religion) with the spirit of Abel (spiritual revelation, signs and wonders). He uses Joel 2:25 as his text, promising that God will restore the years that the locusts have eaten. Branham calls for a return to the power of Pentecost and warns against denominations that deny the supernatural.

title: Enticing Spirits
summary: William Branham warns against 'enticing spirits' that lead believers away from the Word of God, using the biblical account of King Jehoshaphat and the prophet Micaiah to illustrate how false prophets and demonic influences can deceive even sincere people. He emphasizes the need for genuine Holy Ghost conversion over intellectual faith, emotionalism, or worldly substitutes in the church.

title: The Uncertain Sound
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for a certain sound in the Gospel, contrasting the uncertainty of the world with the certainty found in Christ and His Word. He warns against relying on intellectual reasoning rather than the soul's connection to God, and emphasizes the importance of a genuine new birth experience.
themes: The power of the Holy Spirit

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that the faith delivered to the early saints must be contended for today. He contrasts intellectual reasoning with soul-faith, and uses biblical examples to show that God vindicates His Word through supernatural works.

title: Pride
summary: William Branham preaches on the sin of pride, using the story of Simon the Pharisee inviting Jesus to dinner. He contrasts the Pharisee's self-centered motives with Jesus' humility, and warns against acting like a Pharisee—putting on a show rather than being genuine. Branham emphasizes that Jesus takes the lowly place and calls believers to humble themselves.

title: Leading of the Spirit of God
summary: William Branham preaches on being led by the Spirit of God, using the examples of Simeon and Anna who were expecting the Messiah. He contrasts faith and expectation with education and formalism, emphasizing that God's promises are fulfilled to those who believe and are led by the Holy Spirit.

title: Fellowship
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of fellowship with God through the blood of Jesus Christ. He explains that divine healing is part of the atonement and encourages believers to have faith like Abraham, accepting God's promises without doubt. He also contrasts man-made religion with God's provision of the blood sacrifice.

title: Earnestly Contending For The Faith That Was Once Delivered Unto The Saints
summary: William Branham preaches on Jude 3, urging believers to earnestly contend for the original faith delivered to the saints. He emphasizes that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and demonstrates this through prayer for the sick, including discernment of illnesses and visions.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on God's compound redemptive names, focusing on Jehovah-Jireh, meaning 'God will provide Himself a sacrifice.' He uses the story of Abraham and Isaac to illustrate God's provision and faithfulness, and encourages the congregation to believe in God's promises for healing and salvation.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He encourages the congregation to have faith and believe in Jesus as their healer, and demonstrates the gift of discernment through prayer for the sick.

title: Being Led By The Holy Spirit
summary: William Branham speaks on being led by the Holy Spirit, using the example of Simeon who was promised he would see the Christ before he died. He emphasizes that the same Holy Spirit leads believers today, and demonstrates the power of God through healing and discernment.
themes: Being Led by the Holy Spirit

title: The Same Jesus Tonight
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He recounts the story of Lazarus and Martha, highlighting faith in Jesus as the Resurrection and Life. Branham then demonstrates the Holy Spirit's power through words of knowledge and healing, calling the audience to believe in Jesus' presence and power.

title: The Unwelcomed Christ
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Simon the Pharisee and the sinful woman who anointed Jesus' feet, contrasting the Pharisee's lack of hospitality with the woman's loving devotion. He urges believers to give Jesus first place in their lives and not to treat Him as unwelcome.
themes: the value of tears and devotion

title: Sir, We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham shares testimonies of healings and visions, emphasizing that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He calls the audience to have faith in Christ for healing and salvation, demonstrating the gift of discerning spirits and prophecy.

title: The Unwelcomed Christ
summary: William Branham recounts his recent overseas meetings in Switzerland and Germany, describing opposition from state churches and miraculous healings including a blind girl and a deaf-mute man. He defends his ministry against accusations of witchcraft, presents photographic evidence of the Angel of the Lord, and reflects on the need for unity among believers. The sermon then transitions to a dramatic exposition of Luke 7:36-50, focusing on the Pharisee's hidden motives and the sinful woman's love.

title: Prayer Line
summary: William Branham conducts a prayer line, calling out specific ailments and personal details of attendees through the gift of discernment. He emphasizes faith in Jesus Christ for healing and encourages the audience to believe and accept their healing.

title: The Unwelcomed Christ
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Simon the Pharisee inviting Jesus to dinner but failing to welcome Him, contrasting the Pharisee's hypocrisy with the love of a sinful woman who anoints Jesus' feet. He urges believers to genuinely welcome Christ into their hearts and homes, not just invite Him.

title: Faith In Action
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of putting faith into action, using biblical examples like Noah, Moses, David, and Jesus. He encourages believers to trust God's Word wholeheartedly and not rely on intellectual faith alone, emphasizing that God is the same today as in biblical times.

title: Come, Let Us Reason Together
summary: William Branham addresses ministers and laity, explaining the nature of spiritual gifts and visions, emphasizing that gifts are given by God's sovereignty and operate through faith. He uses parables and biblical examples to illustrate how the gift of healing works, and calls for unity and reason among believers.

title: The Power of the Devil
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of the devil, faith, and God, using the Book of Exodus as a foundation. He emphasizes that Satan's dominion ends at death, but God's power of resurrection goes beyond. He calls believers to exercise faith, trust in God's Word, and claim healing through Christ's atonement.

title: A Hidden Life
summary: William Branham speaks on the need for a hidden life with Christ, using the Old Testament tabernacle as a type of the believer's walk from the outer court to the Holy of Holies. He emphasizes entering into the secret place with God, where the veil drops behind and one lives in the Shekinah glory, eating the hidden manna and bearing fruit. He calls ministers to seek this place of adoption and rest in God's presence.

title: The Power of God
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of faith and God's deliverance, using the Exodus account of Moses' mother and the Red Sea crossing as examples. He emphasizes that faith sees beyond death and trials to God's resurrection power, and that God's promises are sure despite opposition.

title: The Power of Decision
summary: William Branham preaches on the power of decision, using the Exodus of Israel as a type of the Church's journey. He emphasizes following the Pillar of Fire (Holy Spirit), living by faith, and partaking of the spiritual manna. He also shares personal experiences of the Holy Spirit's intercession and healing.

title: The Results of Decision
summary: William Branham preaches on the journey of Israel from Egypt to the Promised Land as a type of the Church's spiritual journey. He emphasizes the power of decision, faith, and God's provision, urging believers to cross over into the full blessings of the Gospel rather than remaining on the borderline.

title: The Way To Have Fellowship
summary: William Branham speaks on the necessity of love and fellowship with God through the shed blood of Jesus Christ. He emphasizes that perfect love casts out fear and that true fellowship with God and one another is only possible through the Blood of Christ. He shares personal experiences of how love conquers fear and brings divine protection.

title: A Hidden Life in Christ
summary: William Branham preaches on the necessity of a consecrated, hidden life in Christ, using the Old Testament tabernacle as a type. He contrasts the outer courts and holy place with the Holiest of Holies, where believers can dwell in constant communion with God, bearing lasting fruit.

title: Where I Think Pentecost Failed
summary: William Branham discusses the failure of Pentecostalism, emphasizing the need for a genuine born-again experience over intellectual religion. He critiques organizational stagnation and calls for continued movement with the Holy Spirit, using biblical typology to illustrate spiritual progression.

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that divine healing is part of the atonement and that believers must contend for the faith once delivered to the saints. He shares personal experiences and challenges the church to demonstrate the same works Jesus did, proving His resurrection.

title: The Darkest Hour, Then Jesus Comes Along
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme that in the darkest moments of life, Jesus arrives to bring deliverance. He uses the story of Lazarus, Martha, and Mary to illustrate how Jesus allows trials to deepen before He intervenes, and he explains the operation of spiritual gifts and visions in his ministry.

title: Blind Bartimaeus
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith that stops Jesus amidst the crowd. He contrasts the simplicity of faith in other nations with the skepticism in America, and encourages believers to keep their thoughts positive and focused on Christ.

title: The Calling of Abraham
summary: William Branham preaches on the calling of Abraham from Genesis 12, emphasizing God's sovereign election and unconditional covenant. He contrasts Abraham's faith, which believed God's promise despite natural impossibility, with worldly skepticism, and encourages believers to hold fast to God's Word.

title: Jehovah-Jireh
summary: William Branham preaches on God as Jehovah-Jireh, the Lord who provides a sacrifice, using the story of Abraham and Isaac. He connects this Old Testament name to Jesus Christ and emphasizes that God is the all-sufficient provider for both spiritual and physical needs, including healing. Branham encourages believers to trust in God's promises and lean on His bosom for strength and satisfaction.

title: The Faith of Abraham
summary: William Branham preaches on the faith of Abraham, emphasizing that God's promises are unconditional and that believers must look to God's Word rather than circumstances. He uses Abraham's willingness to sacrifice Isaac as a type of Christ's sacrifice, and declares that God is Jehovah-jireh, the Lord who provides.
themes: the sacrifice of Isaac as a type of Christ

title: Redeemer, Redemption
summary: William Branham preaches on the theme of redemption, using Job 19:25-27 as a text. He illustrates redemption through the story of Ruth and Boaz, emphasizing that Christ is the Redeemer who frees sinners from bondage. Branham encourages believers to stay rooted in Christ and not be swayed by emotionalism or formalism.

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on Hebrews 13:8, emphasizing that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He argues that the same signs and wonders that accompanied Jesus' earthly ministry should be present in the church today, as the Holy Spirit continues His work. Branham calls believers to contend for the faith once delivered to the saints, warning against unbelief and denominational division.

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Jesus, emphasizing that the church must hear and follow Christ alone, not the law or prophets. He calls for a return to God's love and holiness, criticizing modern church worldliness and denominational division.

title: The Arrow of God's Deliverance Shot from a Bow
summary: William Branham preaches on the need for the church to fully receive the Holy Spirit as the arrow of God's deliverance, warning against worldliness and lukewarm faith. He uses the story of King Joash and Elisha to illustrate how the church has struck short of God's blessings, and calls for a return to old-fashioned Holy Ghost revival.

title: Faith Once Delivered to the Saints
summary: William Branham preaches on Jude 3, urging believers to earnestly contend for the faith once delivered to the saints. He emphasizes that true faith comes from God's Word, not creeds or denominations, and shares testimonies of divine healing as evidence of this faith operating today.

title: Stand Still And See The Salvation Of The Lord
summary: William Branham preaches on the need to stand still and see God's salvation, using the story of Jehoshaphat and the invading Moabites. He emphasizes that God displays His power when His people are still and trust His promises, and he demonstrates this through prayer for the sick and words of knowledge.
themes: the same yesterday, today, and forever

title: Have Faith In God
summary: William Branham preaches on the nature of true faith as a substance, not mere emotion or mental conception, using the example of David and Goliath and the fig tree. He emphasizes that faith comes from a personal experience with God and taking Him at His Word, and demonstrates this through a healing service where the Holy Spirit reveals specific conditions.
persons: woman with the issue of blood

title: The Handwriting On The Wall
summary: William Branham preaches on the biblical account of Belshazzar's feast and the handwriting on the wall from Daniel 5, drawing parallels to modern America's spiritual condition. He warns that the nation's sin and rejection of the supernatural message of God will lead to judgment, just as Babylon fell. He calls for repentance and the new birth through the Holy Spirit before the coming Rapture and Tribulation.

title: The Door to the Heart
summary: William Branham preaches on Revelation 3:20, using the metaphor of Jesus knocking at the door of the heart. He emphasizes that while many welcome Jesus as Savior, few allow Him full Lordship, and he urges listeners to open every door of their hearts—including doors of self, selfishness, pride, and faith—to let Christ rule completely.

title: Jesus Christ The Same Yesterday, Today, And Forever
summary: William Branham opens a campaign in Chattanooga, Tennessee, emphasizing that Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He explains that divine healing is a gift to draw sinners, and that the same supernatural manifestations of Jesus' ministry—such as discernment and knowledge of hearts—are available today through the Holy Spirit. He calls believers to recognize the signs of the times and prepare for the Second Coming.
themes: faith in the finished work of Calvary

title: Christ Knocking at the Door
summary: William Branham preaches on Revelation 3:20, emphasizing Christ's knock at the door of the Laodicean church age. He calls believers to open their hearts fully, not just for salvation but for lordship, and warns against spiritual coldness and pride.
themes: Christ knocking at the heart's door
Spiritual coldness and need for eyesalve
Faith in God's Word and power

title: We Would See Jesus
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He uses biblical examples such as Nathanael and the woman at the well to show how Jesus revealed Himself through supernatural knowledge, and challenges the audience to expect the same manifestations today.

title: Behold, I Stand At The Door And Knock
summary: William Branham preaches on Revelation 3:20, emphasizing that Christ stands at the door of the heart and knocks, but the latch is on the inside. He calls for genuine repentance and a return to old-fashioned, Holy Ghost-filled Christianity, addressing issues of worldliness, pride, and lukewarmness in the Laodicean church age.
themes: Christ knocking at the heart's door

title: Looking At The Unseen
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of living by faith rather than by sight, using biblical examples like Abraham, Moses, Joshua, and Elisha to illustrate how looking at the unseen God enables believers to overcome barriers of unbelief and receive His promises. He encourages the congregation to pass the 'sound barrier' of doubt and enter into the freedom of faith, where healing and salvation are realized.

title: Be Certain of God
summary: William Branham preaches on the certainty of God using the story of the widow of Zarephath and Elijah. He emphasizes that God tests faith, and believers must hold onto His Word even in desperate circumstances. The sermon calls for absolute trust in God's promises for salvation, healing, and the Holy Spirit.
themes: the Holy Spirit and the Word

title: Conference With God
summary: William Branham speaks on the importance of holding a conference with God, drawing parallels between earthly conferences and divine meetings. He uses biblical examples such as Moses at the burning bush and the Red Sea, and the incarnation of Christ, to illustrate how God calls His people to reason together and make decisions in crucial moments.

title: Believest Thou This?
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of Lazarus, emphasizing that when Jesus leaves a home or church, trouble follows. He calls the church to return to Pentecostal power and demonstrates faith through a testimony of a baby's healing.
themes: the role of women in the church

title: Hear Ye Him
summary: William Branham preaches on the transfiguration of Jesus, emphasizing the command 'Hear Ye Him' as the ultimate authority. He contrasts human values with divine values, using the parable of a valuable stamp and the story of Abraham Lincoln's pardon to illustrate that God's Word must be received as a pardon to be effective. He calls the church to reflect Christ and warns against substituting the Holy Spirit's guidance with human traditions.

title: Be Not Afraid, It Is I
summary: William Branham preaches on the importance of simple faith in Jesus Christ, using the biblical account of Jesus walking on water and the disciples' fear. He shares testimonies of miraculous healings among Native Americans and emphasizes that Jesus is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and that believers should not be afraid but trust in Him.

title: Jesus Christ the Same Yesterday, Today, and Forever
summary: William Branham preaches on the unchanging nature of Jesus Christ, emphasizing that He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. He discusses divine healing as a finished work at Calvary, the importance of faith and confession, and the need for believers to see Jesus through the Holy Spirit's manifestation in the church.

title: Thou Son Of David, Have Mercy On Me
summary: William Branham preaches on the story of blind Bartimaeus, emphasizing faith as the sixth sense that defies the five physical senses. He encourages persistent faith and prayer, drawing parallels between Bartimaeus's hope and the believer's trust in God's unchanging power.
